Formulation
- Predisposing factors:
  - Type 2 diabetes mellitus, overweight, hypertension, alcohol and tobacco use may predispose to more severe intercurrent illness.
- Precipitating factors:
  - Recent social exposure (dining out celebration five days prior) and subsequent acute onset of respiratory symptoms.
- Perpetuating factors:
  - Continued activity (work, attending/engaging with football), sleep disturbance from feverish episodes, alcohol use and smoking that may delay recovery.
- Protective factors:
  - Living with spouse, employment, willingness to reduce smoking, and engagement with GP advice.
- Summary:
  - A middle-aged man with type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents with a 4–5 day history of an acute viral respiratory illness (dry cough worse in morning, sore throat, systemic symptoms including sweats/feverish sensations, mild diarrheal episode initially, generalized stiffness, subjective shortness of breath). He reports feeling run-down and has some sleep disturbance. No mental health diagnoses, suicidality, or self-harm disclosed. Management focused on symptomatic care, delayed antibiotic strategy, and safety-netting with review if no improvement.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Acute viral respiratory illness with associated functional impact (feeling run-down, disturbed sleep)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Recover from current illness and return to usual function/work.
  - Improve sleep and reduce breathlessness.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Symptom resolution within expected time course for viral illness.
  - Prevent secondary bacterial infection; monitor and treat if indicated.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Rest and avoid strenuous activity as tolerated.
  - Maintain adequate oral fluids.
  - Take regular paracetamol for fever/aches as needed (advice given).
  - Monitor symptoms, particularly breathlessness and fevers.
  - Start delayed course of prescribed antibiotics (amoxicillin) if symptoms do not improve in 24–48 hours or worsen.
  - Return for review if breathlessness worsens or no improvement by one week.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provided symptomatic advice (rest, fluids, paracetamol).
  - Offered delayed antibiotic prescription: Amoxicillin — oral, one tablet three times a day; dose not documented (patient instructed to start if not improving in 24–48 hours).
  - Safety-netting: advise review if persistent/worsening shortness of breath or if not better by one week.
  - No immediate antibiotics indicated; clinician to review in clinic if symptoms persist.

Secondary Problem: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension (comorbid medical conditions)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Continue usual management of diabetes and blood pressure during acute illness.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Ensure comorbidities are managed and do not complicate recovery from acute illness.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Continue prescribed medications (Metformin, Lisinopril) as usual unless advised otherwise by clinician.
  - Maintain hydration and monitoring of glucose as per usual plan (if applicable).
  - Minimize alcohol while unwell.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Confirm current medication doses at follow-up (doses not documented in this consultation).
  - Reinforce general advice about alcohol reduction and smoking cessation as part of long-term risk reduction.
  - Arrange review if acute illness affects glucose control or blood pressure.

Tertiary Problem: Alcohol and tobacco use; psychosocial stressor (marital friction)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce alcohol intake and smoking; improve sleep and relationship stress where possible.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Support smoking reduction/cessation and safer alcohol intake.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Continue attempts to reduce cigarette use using vaporiser; consider formal cessation support.
  - Monitor alcohol consumption and consider reducing weekly intake.
  - Use coping strategies (rest, limit shouting at football if affecting voice/sleep).
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Offer brief advice on smoking cessation and signposting to cessation services (not documented as completed in this consult).
  - Offer brief counseling on alcohol intake and referral to specialist services if patient requests (not documented as completed).
  - Consider assessment/referral for psychosocial support if marital stress worsens or mood changes develop (not recorded as needed at this visit).

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Nature of likely viral illness; expected course.
  - Self-care: rest, fluids, paracetamol for fever/aches.
  - Safety-netting and when to start delayed antibiotics (amoxicillin) and when to re-present.
  - Advice to monitor breathlessness and fever, and to seek review if not improved by one week.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Increasing or worsening shortness of breath.
  - High or persistent fevers.
  - No clinical improvement within 24–48 hours prompting initiation of antibiotics, or no improvement by one week requiring re-evaluation.
- Coping Strategies:
  - Rest, fluid intake, pacing activity.
  - Use of paracetamol for symptomatic relief.
  - Reduce alcohol intake while unwell; continue efforts to reduce smoking.

- Patient Consent to Plan:
  - Verbal agreement to the management plan and delayed antibiotic strategy recorded in consultation.
